newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures trade slightly off on quiet day.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures trade slightly off on quiet day.

text.p: U.S. debt futures ended mostly lower on Monday in very quiet trading.
One Eurodollar futures trader called himself "cautiously bearish" and looked for more downside risk than upside potential this week, with little fundamental news expected.

"I tend to be still kind of holding on a cautiously bearish stance at this point. People are pretty bulled up on the market.... It doesn't mean there's no more upside, but I think the risk is that there's some kind of a 10 or 15 basis point flush out to the downside," the trader said.
"I don't think you'll see much more than that," he said.
On the upside, he said, "maybe the market grinds up, maybe another three or four basis points."
After an intraday high early in the morning at 115-07/32, U.S. 30-year Treasury bond futures drifted in a narrow range and briefly fell below support at 114-20/32.

One T-bond trader said the market was looking forward to any hints on U.S. monetary policy from two U.S. Federal Reserve officials on Tuesday. Chairman Alan Greenspan is scheduled to hold a press conference in Tokyo at 9:30 a.m. Tuesday (0030 GMT Tuesday, 1930 EST Monday), and Fed governor Lawrence Lindsey is scheduled to speak in Washington at 1400 EST/1900 GMT.

The National Association of Home Builders reported after midday that its index fell to 51 for November, down from a revised 55. It was exactly as some traders had forecast and had little impact on the market, traders said. On Tuesday, U.S. October housing starts are forecast to come in at an annualized 1.443 million units, compared to 1.438 million for September.

"There's not much to say for the rest of week unless people holding long positions get a little bit squirrely for whatever reason and maybe sell off the market a little, but we've certainly had no indication of that so far," the Euros trader said, calling Monday's trading "pretty anemic."

On the day, December T-bonds were down 03/32 at 114-27/32, 10-year notes were off 03/32 at 110-19/32, March Eurodollars were unchanged at 94.49 and December Eurodollars were steady at 94.50. -Derivatives Desk(312)408-8750/E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
